newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU calls for self-regulation of Internet.
newsitem.headline: EU calls for self-regulation of Internet.

text.p: European Union countries should promote self-regulation and ratings systems to control illegal and harmful material on the Internet, EU telecommunications ministers said on Thursday.

The ministers echoed the approach proposed last month by the European Commission, which shied away from advocating strict new legislation to protect children or prevent criminals from misusing the global computer network.
They said in a statement that EU governments should promote solutions such as industry codes of conduct, self-regulatory bodies and hotlines for the public.

They should also encourage the use of technologies such as the Platform for Internet Content Selection (PICS), which allows Internet users to filter out sexually explicit or other unwanted material through the use of ratings systems, the ministers said.
The ministers also asked the Commission to examine the question of legal liability.

The EU executive said in its own report that governments should consider whether an EU legal framework was needed to clarify whether companies that offer Internet acess or services were liable for illegal content such as child pornography, copyright infringements, libel or fraudulent material.

The statement also said EU governments should promote international cooperation on the question of harmful and illegal Internet content and participate actively in a global ministerial conference on the issue that Germany plans to host.
